components.name: Address capsule
components.description: Documentation-only approximation of the native address field. Display host until focused; edit the full URL. Privacy and reload controls move to the menu at accessibility sizes. Native address glass uses 65% black tint in dark appearance, clear tint in light appearance, and opaque secondarySystemBackground under Reduce Transparency. Shared identity morphs into the compact site pill.

components.name: Unified browser row
components.description: Documentation-only structural approximation of native SwiftUI. Back, address, tabs and menu share one row of separate glass capsules. Native glass, SF Symbols and Dynamic Type require iOS verification. Address editing occupies the row; secondary actions live in the menu.
components.css: .ds-nav{display:flex;gap:6px;padding:4px 12px;font:15px system-ui}.ds-nav button,.ds-nav input{min-height:48px;border:0;border-radius:99px;background:ButtonFace;color:ButtonText;font:inherit}.ds-nav button{flex:0 0 44px;padding:0}.ds-nav input{min-width:30px;width:100%;padding:0 14px}.ds-nav span{display:inline-grid;place-items:center;width:24px;height:24px;border:1.8px solid currentColor;border-radius:5px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-nav button:hover{opacity:.8}.ds-nav button:active{opacity:.6}.ds-nav :focus-visible{outline:2px solid Highlight;outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Profile unlock action
components.description: Documentation-only HTML approximation of the native prominent capsule button. SwiftUI owns tint, disabled appearance, Dynamic Type and progress rendering; validate these on iOS. The secondary Switch profile action opens the native Profiles sheet.

components.name: Browser menu
components.description: Documentation-only content approximation of the native bottom-right Menu. Share appears only for a URL; media and download actions appear when available. Forward and Reload can be disabled. Native menu owns presentation, scrolling and dismissal.
components.css: .ds-menu{display:grid;max-width:280px;padding:8px;border-radius:24px;background:Canvas;color:CanvasText;font:16px system-ui}.ds-menu button{min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:8px 16px;border:0;background:transparent;color:inherit;font:inherit}.ds-menu hr{width:90%;border:0;border-top:1px solid GrayText}.ds-menu button:hover:not(:disabled){background:ButtonFace;border-radius:12px}.ds-menu button:active:not(:disabled){opacity:.7}.ds-menu button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid Highlight}.ds-menu button:disabled{opacity:.4}

components.name: Bookmark name suggestion
components.description: Documentation-only HTML approximation of the native inline suggestion. SwiftUI uses subheadline text, a 10pt vertical stack, 4pt vertical padding and borderless actions with a 44pt minimum height. Generating shows progress; unavailable keeps the name unchanged and offers Dismiss. Use name requires explicit acceptance; in the rename form it fills the draft until Save. Example content is not production user data. Validate semantic colors and Dynamic Type on iOS.

components.css: .ds-suggestion{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;padding:4px 0;color:CanvasText;font:15px system-ui}.ds-suggestion button{min-height:44px;text-align:left;border:0;padding:0;background:transparent;color:LinkText;font:inherit}.ds-suggestion button:hover{opacity:.8}.ds-suggestion button:active{opacity:.6}.ds-suggestion button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid Highlight;outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Compact site pill
components.description: Documentation-only native restore control approximation. Caption2 medium capped at xxxLarge, 10pt horizontal and 3pt vertical padding, maximum width 112pt (180pt at accessibility sizes), minimum 44pt target extending upward. Bottom lowering is min(12, max(0, safeAreaBottom - 20)). Tap restores controls without focusing the address. Native dark tint is 65% black; Reduce Transparency uses opaque semantic background.

narrative.overview:
Harbor combines a calm maritime identity with native iOS behavior. Deep blue water, reflected warm sunlight and the supplied Harbor mark establish the start page and locked profile screen; semantic content surfaces and native Liquid Glass keep everyday browsing clear. Collections remains a reference for future organization, not a second identity or an implemented groups feature.

This is the implemented SwiftUI system, extracted from `Harbor/Views/HarborTheme.swift`, `StartPage.swift`, `BrowserView.swift`, `TabSwitcherView.swift`, `LibraryViews.swift` and `ProfilesView.swift`. The [identity board](design/brand/harbor-identity.png) remains brand authority. The Xcode project references `assets/HarborIcon/Harbor.icon` directly; the in-app mark draws the supplied SVG path geometry in a resolution-independent Canvas. Generated comp marks never replace the supplied identity. Surface behavior belongs in [the browser brief](design/BROWSER-SURFACE.md).
keyCharacteristics: Still Horizon artwork at the start of browsing and while a profile is locked.
Native semantic content and glass controls.
Inter branding with system functional typography.
Honest personal content and accessible reflow.

rules.name: The Semantic Content Rule
rules.body: Use native adaptive colors for readable functional content; keep the scenery palette in Harbor-owned artwork and deliberate brand moments.

rules.name: The Brand Type Rule
rules.body: Reserve Inter for Harbor branding; use Dynamic Type system styles for working controls and content. Toolbar symbols are capped at `.xxxLarge` while text and accessible names remain available.

rules.name: The Native Material Rule
rules.body: Keep glass in the control layer and content on stable semantic surfaces. Do not replace native material behavior with fixed blur/shadow recipes. Horizon artwork is still; there is no ambient animation to disable.

dos: Do preserve the Harbor mark and supplied palette.
Do keep glass in the control/navigation layer and content legible beneath it.
Do make selection and protection states understandable without color alone.
Do keep locked profiles visually consistent with Harbor while withholding browsing content.
Do support light mode, dark mode, Dynamic Type and accessibility appearance settings.
Do keep privacy language factual: tracker blocking does not mean incognito or complete anonymity.
donts: Don't copy generated sample sites, favorites or counts into real user data.
Don't add inactive group controls before groups exist.
Don't carry mockup microphone icons into scope without an explicit voice-input decision.
Don't invent fixed blur, shadow or layout tokens from an illustration.
